project.name: Shop Checkout
project.description: Checkout that answers in milliseconds, charges cards exactly once and never loses an event.

groups.name: Vercel
groups.description: Storefront hosted on Vercel; server actions run on its Node.js runtime.

groups.name: AWS us-east-1
groups.description: ECS services and workers next to RDS Postgres and ElastiCache Redis, in one VPC.

nodes.name: Customer
nodes.summary: Shops on the storefront, pays for a cart and receives the confirmation email.

nodes.name: Web app
nodes.summary: Renders the checkout page and places the order through a server action.
nodes.description:
Stripe's `PaymentElement` tokenizes the card in the browser, so only a `paymentMethodId` reaches our servers.

The page renders one `idempotencyKey` per form and the `placeOrder` server action sends it as the `idempotency-key` header. A double click or a retried submit therefore reuses the same key, and the API replays the first answer instead of creating a second order.

nodes.name: Orders API
nodes.summary: Owns the order lifecycle: accepts orders, records Stripe outcomes and writes every event to the outbox.
nodes.description:
**The only writer of the `Order` table.** Every state change commits together with the `OutboxEvent` that announces it, so no event is lost and none is sent for a rolled-back change.

- `POST /orders` validates the body with zod, claims the `idempotency-key` in Redis, then in one transaction copies the cart into an `Order` (`PENDING_PAYMENT`) and writes a `payment.process` outbox row. It answers `202 Accepted` without waiting for Stripe.
- `POST /webhooks/stripe` verifies the signature on the raw body and, in one transaction, records the event id in `ProcessedStripeEvent`, moves the order to `CONFIRMED` or `FAILED` and writes `order.confirmed`. A redelivered event hits the primary key and is acknowledged without side effects.

nodes.name: Outbox relay
nodes.summary: Publishes committed outbox rows to the payments queue and the order events stream.
nodes.description:
Polls `OutboxEvent` in batches of 50 with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, so several replicas can run without publishing the same row twice at the same time. Each row is published, then marked `publishedAt` in the same transaction.

Delivery is **at least once**: a crash between publishing and committing sends the row again. Consumers are built for it: the payment job uses the order id as `jobId`, and Stripe dedupes on the same key.

nodes.name: Payment worker
nodes.summary: Charges the card by creating a Stripe PaymentIntent for each payment job.
nodes.description:
Creates and confirms the PaymentIntent with `idempotencyKey` set to the order id, so BullMQ retries and re-published jobs always map to one charge. It never writes the order: Stripe's webhook is the source of truth for the outcome.

- Network and `5xx` errors throw, and BullMQ retries up to 5 times with exponential backoff from 2 s.
- A declined card throws `UnrecoverableError`, because retrying cannot help; the `payment_intent.payment_failed` webhook marks the order `FAILED`.

nodes.name: Notifications worker
nodes.summary: Sends the order confirmation email for every order.confirmed event.
nodes.description:
Reads `orders:events` as the `notifications` consumer group, loads the order and its items, and sends the Postmark template `order-confirmed`. It acknowledges with `XACK` only after Postmark accepts the email; a crashed consumer's pending messages are reclaimed with `XAUTOCLAIM`.

Delivery is at least once, so a crash between sending and `XACK` can send a second email.

nodes.name: Payments queue
nodes.summary: Holds one payment.process job per order until the payment worker charges it.
nodes.description: BullMQ queue `payments` on Redis. Jobs use the order id as `jobId`, retry 5 times with exponential backoff and are kept for 24 hours after completion, which is the window in which a re-published job is ignored.

nodes.name: Order events
nodes.summary: Streams order.confirmed events to every consumer group that needs them.
nodes.description: Redis stream `orders:events`, capped at about 100,000 entries with `MAXLEN ~`. Each consumer group keeps its own position, so adding a new consumer (analytics, fulfilment) needs no change in the Orders API.

nodes.name: Postgres
nodes.summary: Stores orders, their items, the outbox and the Stripe events already processed.
nodes.description: System of record. Tables: `Order` and `OrderItem` (written only by the Orders API), `OutboxEvent` (written by the Orders API, claimed by the relay, indexed on `publishedAt, id`) and `ProcessedStripeEvent` (one row per Stripe event id).

nodes.name: Redis
nodes.summary: Keeps idempotency keys and the responses replayed to retried requests.
nodes.description: `idem:<key>` holds `pending` while a request runs, then the stored response, for 24 hours. The same instance backs the payments queue and the order events stream, so it runs with append-only persistence.

nodes.name: Stripe
nodes.summary: Charges the card and reports the outcome through signed webhooks.

nodes.name: Postmark
nodes.summary: Renders the order-confirmed template and delivers the email.

edges.label: POST /orders
edges.description: Server-to-server call from `placeOrder`, with the form's `idempotency-key` header. A `409` means the same key is still being processed; a repeated key after success replays the original `202` body.

edges.label: SET idem:* NX
edges.description: `SET NX EX 86400` claims the key; a failed transaction deletes it so the client can retry with the same key.

edges.label: orders + outbox
edges.description: Every write is one transaction that changes `Order` and inserts the matching `OutboxEvent`.

edges.label: XREADGROUP
edges.description: Consumer group `notifications`, batches of 10, blocking for up to 5 s. Messages stay pending until `XACK`.

edges.label: POST /v1/payment_intents
edges.description: Sent with `Idempotency-Key: ord_42` (the order id), so Stripe returns the same PaymentIntent for every retry within 24 hours.

edges.label: POST /webhooks/stripe
edges.description: Mounted with `express.raw()` before the JSON parser, because `constructEvent` checks the `stripe-signature` header against the exact bytes. An invalid signature gets `400`; anything else that was stored gets `200`, which stops Stripe's retries.

flows.name: Checkout
flows.summary: The customer pays for a cart. The order and its payment job commit together, the API answers 202, and the relay hands the job to the worker that charges Stripe.
flows.trigger: Customer clicks "Pay" on the checkout page

steps.title: Customer submits the checkout form
steps.description: Stripe.js has already turned the card into a `paymentMethodId`; the form also carries the idempotency key rendered with the page.

steps.title: API claims the idempotency key
steps.description: If the key is already `pending` the API answers `409`; if it holds a response, the API replays it and stops here.

steps.title: API commits the order and its outbox row
steps.description: **One transaction**: either the order and its `payment.process` event both exist, or neither does. No broker call happens inside the request.

steps.title: API answers 202 Accepted
steps.description: The customer sees the order page right away; the charge happens in the background.

steps.title: Relay claims the pending outbox row
steps.description: Rows locked by another relay replica are skipped, not waited for.

payload.select: WHERE "publishedAt" IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 50 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED

steps.title: Relay enqueues the payment.process job
steps.description: `jobId` is the order id, so publishing the same row twice leaves one job.

steps.title: Payment worker picks up the job
Worker creates the PaymentIntent on Stripe
steps.description: Sent with `Idempotency-Key: ord_42`, so a retried job gets the same PaymentIntent instead of a second charge.

steps.title: Stripe returns the PaymentIntent
steps.description: The worker completes the job but does not touch the order: the webhook decides whether it is paid.

flows.name: Payment confirmation
flows.summary: Stripe reports the successful charge. The API confirms the order and writes order.confirmed in one transaction, and the relay appends it to the order events stream.

steps.title: Stripe sends payment_intent.succeeded
steps.description: The API verifies the `stripe-signature` header against the raw body before reading anything.

steps.title: API confirms the order in one transaction
steps.description: Inserting the event id first makes a redelivery fail on the primary key and change nothing. The update only matches `PENDING_PAYMENT`, so a late or out-of-order event cannot move a final status.

steps.title: API acknowledges with 200
steps.description: Stripe stops retrying. Duplicates get `200` as well, since they were already handled.

payload.select: WHERE "publishedAt" IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 50 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED

steps.title: Relay appends order.confirmed to the stream

flows.name: Confirmation email
flows.summary: The notifications worker reads order.confirmed from the stream, loads the order and sends the confirmation through Postmark.

steps.title: Worker loads the order and its items
Worker acknowledges the message with XACK
steps.description: Only after Postmark accepted the email. Until then the message stays pending and another consumer can reclaim it.
